in_hebrew.name: כָסְפָר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'kaphar' meaning 'to hide, to cover'. The name Kaspar is derived from the word 'kaspa' meaning 'box, chest, treasury'. This name is biblical and refers to a wise man from the East who came to worship the infant Jesus (Matthew 2:1-12).

data.cultural_impact: In Christian tradition, Kaspar is revered as one of the Three Wise Men, the Magi who followed a star to Bethlehem and brought gifts to the infant Jesus. The name Kaspar has therefore come to symbolize travel, adventure, and the pursuit of knowledge, with its association with the Magi's journey.
data.spiritual_significance: Kaspar is a reminder of the spiritual journey we each embark on in life, seeking the truth and wisdom that can only be found through faith and following the guidance of God, like the Magi followed the star. It is a name that instills a sense of purpose and direction, leading us on our own personal pilgrimage to knowledge, understanding, and ultimately, enlightenment.
